public_rationale: Anthropic doubled Claude Code's five-hour allowances on existing Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans effective May 6. That is a direct counterexample to the forecast that rate limits would not be eased. This finding does not establish falling provider costs or permanent improvements across every service.
limitations: The finding concerns the rate-limit branch.
It establishes an announced effective policy change, not uniform experience for every account.
A later reversal would not erase this intervening easing.

our_interpretation: Read this as a categorical forecast about customer prices and service access at OpenAI and Anthropic, rather than a claim about the author's private mental state.
An actual increase in included usage on an existing plan counts as easing a rate limit. Merely purchasing a more expensive plan does not.
A verified easing by either company contradicts the categorical exclusion. No price reduction is also required.
criteria.support_condition: No finite observation period establishes the indefinite assertion that prices or rate limits will never improve.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After April 14, 2026, either company implements a like-for-like service price reduction or increases included usage allowances on an existing plan.
